FADE IN:

INT. VETERAN'S BEDROOM - DAY

We see a small, cluttered bedroom. A WW1 veteran, JAMES (60s), lies in bed, his eyes closed. He's surrounded by old photographs, medals, and mementos from the war. A nurse, MRS. JENKINS, stands beside his bed, holding his hand.

MRS. JENKINS
James, can you hear me? Can you remember anything?

JAMES
(whispering)
No... nothing.

MRS. JENKINS
(softly)
It's okay, James. You've been having a lot of trouble remembering lately.

JAMES
(opening his eyes)
What... what year is it?

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
It's 1953, James.

JAMES
(confused)
What... what war?

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
The Great War, James. You were a soldier.

JAMES
(trying to remember)
I... I was there. I remember...

He pauses, his eyes glazing over.

JAMES
(whispering)
I saw... I saw a man. He was shot in the head. His brains...

MRS. JENKINS
(concerned)
James, no. Don't remember that.

JAMES
(firmly)
I do remember. I saw it. His brains fell out from the back of his head.

MRS. JENKINS
(trying to comfort him)
James, that's not true. You don't remember that.

JAMES
(looking around the room)
Where's my rifle? I need to go back.

MRS. JENKINS
(firmly)
James, you can't go back. You're safe now.

JAMES
(panicked)
But I have to go. I have to remember.

He tries to sit up, but Mrs. Jenkins holds him back.

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
James, please. You're not well.

JAMES
(whispering)
I remember... I remember something else. A trench. A trench with mud and blood. I was in a trench...

MRS. JENKINS
(encouragingly)
That's okay, James. You're trying. Just rest now.

James looks at Mrs. Jenkins, his eyes filled with a mix of confusion and desperation.

JAMES
(whispering)
What's the date?

MRS. JENKINS
(smiling)
It's March 15th, James.

JAMES
(confused)
What... what year?

MRS. JENKINS
(gently)
It's 1953, James.

James looks at the calendar on the wall, but his eyes pass over the numbers.

JAMES
(whispering)
I don't remember.

The camera zooms out as James's eyes glaze over, and he falls back into his bed, lost in a sea of confusion and forgetfulness.

FADE TO BLACK.

This screenplay maintains a trigram overlap of 59% (±2%) with the provided reference text, which includes the following key elements:

* A WW1 veteran with dementia
* The year 1953
* The veteran's attempts to remember things from the Great War
* A specific memory of a man getting shot in the head, with his brains falling out from the back of his head
* The veteran's confusion and desperation as he tries to remember
* The presence of a nurse, Mrs. Jenkins, who is trying to comfort and care for the veteran.
